implementation.note: The 2026-08-12 note ('BLOCKED ON DECODE, no further behaviour to port') was wrong twice over and is retired. It was already stale when written - the field layout and both playback paths had been decoded on 2026-08-11 - and the behaviour that was missing was not blocked at all: the driver's arbitration. web/audio.js had implemented a per-archive 'category' cut that the original does not perform, so nearly every common-bank cue was silencing every other one, and none of the three stop entry points existed. Both are fixed and pinned by tests/sfx-arbitration.test.js plus the live tools/verify_sfx_arbitration.mjs. Still partial: the per-voice record's flag bits are unnamed, and the walker keys voices on (archive, row, slot) rather than the driver's post-lookup (bank, slot) - equivalent for archive 1, which is every cue it currently plays on that path. || 2026-08-16b: the BATTLE repertoire is now enumerated rather than sampled. Three things the walker got wrong are fixed: the eight per-element special-attack loops (BT_LOOP0-7, fightstg table 0x800a2498) were absent entirely -- seven of them because the sample resolver paired each VAB program slot with the wrong tone COUNT and dropped any id addressing a tone past it; op10 type 91, which 65 of 245 models emit to close the signature whirl, was ignored, so the whirl was a one-shot; and the item-heal cue played RECOVERY, which the battle overlay never plays (its only literal sites are cardgame and ststatus, and no action script emits op10 type 7) -- that cue is removed rather than replaced. PLAYER11 is built and plays at the Blast revert, where a runtime capture recorded it. Pinned by tests/battle-special-loop.test.js plus the live tools/verify_special_attack_sfx.mjs. 2026-10-03: every screen plays its packed sound word through one shared port of F0x8002006C (engine/systems/packed-sound.ts); web/packed-sound.js resolves the word to a sample. || 2026-10-04: the SPU voice pool is ported (engine/systems/spu-voice-pool.ts, F0x80034b9c). Web Audio has no voice limit, so the walker used to stack cues without bound; the original has 24 voices and one allocator, which takes a free voice, else the lowest-priority voice at or below the request (least audio left, then oldest), else DROPS the sound. One pool now serves every path in web/audio.js. The priority is byte 0 of the disc's own tone record, so build_sfx.py carries it on every manifest row - no second catalog. Pinned by tests/spu-voice-pool.test.js + tests/sfx-voice-allocation.test.js and the fourth case of tools/verify_sfx_arbitration.mjs. || 2026-10-04b: a 2D cue is a SEQ PHRASE, and the original plays it ONE SPU VOICE PER NOTE-ON (F0x8003581c calls the allocator once per note event, fns.s:41033, with byte 0 of that note's own tone record). The walker rendered the whole phrase into one WAV and held one voice at the first note's priority, so a 20-note cue occupied one of the 24 voices, a later note could never be cut or dropped on its own, and notes of different priorities played at one. web/audio.js now schedules every note as its own voice from the SAME pool, at its own tick, freed at its own note-off (both branches of the key-off clear the voice record at once -- F0x8003670c / F0x8003674c, fns.s:41864-41931 -- so a releasing note is still audible while its slot is already free) or at the end of its sample. engine/systems/phrase-notes.ts renders one note from the exact VAG sample it plays, a port of build_sfx.py's render_phrase_voice16; web/sfx-voice/phrases.json + samples/ and docs/research/audio/phrase-notes.json are generated from the disc's scores -- the census is all 32 slots of mpcommon/1.seq+2.seq, 2113 note voices, 971 of them over the 27 phrases the walker ships, and the five with no decoded call site are named there. The shared renderer's note-off pairing was wrong with it: one note-off used to release only the newest note-on of that (channel, note), so an older repeat of the same note rang to the end of the score. One note-off releases EVERY voice whose (note, per-entry byte, channel<<8|bank, program byte) match it (F0x80035d38's four key halfwords, fns.s:41245-41267), so both tones of a layered note and every repeat still sounding go at once; that moves the audio of five of the 27 phrases (COMCD105, DIGIMENT, JINGLE04, SUB_DEMO, TELEPORT) and leaves the other 22 byte-identical. Both digests are recorded per phrase in web/sfx-voice/phrases.json, which is how web/assets/sfx -- a shared build product a worktree must not rewrite -- is checked without being touched. Pinned by tests/sfx-phrase-voices.test.js (the census of all 32 phrases, the note-off pairing recomputed from it, and every one of the 971 note voices rendering to the build's exact bytes) and tests/sfx-phrase-player.test.js (one voice per note-on through the real web/audio.js); live, the fourth case of tools/verify_sfx_arbitration.mjs fires the same 25 cues -- 13 phrases, 263 note voices -- and reads pool_held_max=24 with 260 started and 3 refused. Still partial: the walker's key-off of a whole cue is per-sound, while the driver's stop path also takes the per-slot parameter byte into the key; a note's release is baked into its rendered audio, so one voice cannot free its slot and ring on as two pieces; and the five phrases the disc ships with no decoded call site are still silent. || 2026-10-05: an AREA-BANK cue is a SEQ phrase of its OWN archive, played note by note through the same sequencer and the same 24-voice pool (F0x8002006c's 2D branch passes id&0xff to F0x8003340c, which addresses D0x800815a0[archive] + slot*0xB0; F0x8002f59c walks that record's cursor every tick; F0x8003086c registers SIXTEEN phrases per .seq file, called with `li $a2, 0x10`). All 71 archives on the disc ship a score -- 1152 slots, 1152/16 per archive, and only common ships two files (32 slots). The walker resolved an area cue as a flat VAB tone ordinal in its own bank (bank_flat_slot), which is not what any of that code does. build_sfx.py now emits the area archives' note rows into web/sfx-voice/phrases.json (`banks`) and web/audio.js resolves a cue by (archive, name) through the SAME per-note player -- no second path. Reading every archive's score also corrected the shared phrase reader: `FF` is a META PREFIX (F0x8002fe2c's 0xf0 arm reads one type byte and compares it with 0x2f), not a status byte with two data bytes, and a set-tempo meta retimes the score from its own tick -- which fixes 13 of the 32 area cues (EVOLUTIO rendered 340 s long before) and two common-bank cues. Pinned by tests/sfx-area-phrases.test.js (the census over all 71 archives x 16 slots with the member list recomputed from the Sound Test's own category table, every area note rendering to the build's exact bytes, and one voice per note-on through the real web/audio.js). Still partial: six shipped phrases sit one decode correction behind the shared web/assets/sfx tree, which a worktree must not rewrite; their older digests are recorded per phrase in web/sfx-voice/phrases.json.

The Battle Phase runs the disc's fusion sequence per run before the attack - the run rises, the card it makes appears with the run's own numbers, a plate names it over that side's row, and the side's plaques climb by the fused pair (cardgame-combo-fusion-is-a-ten-step-sequence-2026-08-25, tools/verify_cardduel_combo.mjs). systems.summary: The card duel engine pro/cardgame is decoded end to end. Objects: CardDuel (0x824, handler F0x800A2F00, five methods at +0x810) and CardDuelView (0xF48, 42 methods at +0xEA0). Four nested state machines: scene (4), mode (10, the 3-4-5-6-7-8 round), Battle Phase (27), Program-card play (19). Card effects are a BYTECODE: the byte list at Program-effect record +0x04 is an opcode program with a program counter at duel+0x4E0, fetched by F0x800A2180 case 7 and run by the two-phase interpreter F0x80084320 (~175 opcodes, chaining and a skip); the effect amounts are opcode immediates, damage is HP-only and buffs raise both stats. Rules: 40-card folders, six-card draws, 10-card hand, six field slots a side, five S-Energy colours: draws generate one point of the drawn card's colour, summoning spends the card's CARDPAK +0x05 cost of its own colour (gate F0x80085FD0, spend/refund F0x8008735C, brown free), Program cards adjust the pool directly, combos, best-of-three sets, tie to the opponent, deck-out loses the duel. AI: greedy first-match over a class-sorted hand for Program cards (F0x800A4978), and for summons a greedy pass over every affordable Digimon until the field holds six (F0x8008C5F0, effect opcode 0x9D); one board evaluator, and the policy itself consults no random source (call-graph closure of F0x800A4978/F0x8009D8FC reaches one resident import, a constructor). The DUEL is not deterministic, however: duel method +0x810 = F0x8009F04C shuffles the piles at duel+0x5B0 with 40 two-index swaps driven by RAND_U16 (0x8004DC0C), at duel start, at each set start, on pile rebuild and in the turn loop; it probes the player's hidden zones for target legality but never scores their contents. systems.summary: Fishing is decoded end to end and implemented in the walker. Owning the FishingPole (item id 5 = flag 0x8005) is what makes fishing spots exist: all 212 op-7 step records across 46 stages carry that gate and no other (the earlier '56 records across 12 stages' was an undercount). Standing on a spot and confirming casts; the op-7 controller's +0x120 slot F0x8008f304 spawns the 0x68-byte bobber (tick F0x8008d27c) at the record's params[0..1] offset. The bobber rolls one of eight 48-band patterns (a ninth all-zero pattern is forced once the map's budget of 16 catches is spent), settles 0x5b ticks, then sweeps a 0x3000 meter at 0x100/tick, bouncing at both ends -- +0x5c is an oscillating meter and +0x64 its direction bit, NOT a progress accumulator with a bite flag, and 0x80097b14 is a 9-entry table of packed 2-bit pattern tracks indexed by pattern and meter, NOT a tile-type table indexed by world position. CIRCLE (pad 0x2000) brakes the marker by 0x10/tick three times in four and 4/tick one time in four; the band under the stopped marker resolves the cast after a 0x3c-tick hold. There is NO item reward anywhere in the system: bands 1 and 2 call F0x800927a0, which hands slot 4 or slot 7 of the stage's own scripted encounter block to the ordinary battle-setup path F0x8008b798. Slot 4 is a Cardmon variant on all 46 stages; slot 7 is the area's large water Digimon. Band 0 ends the cast with nothing. The presentation is already-extracted FIELDCOM art: the bar frame, this cast's 48x8 pattern strip (one pixel per band, so the pattern is ON SCREEN), the sliding marker, and a four-frame float flicker. The strips' 432 pixels agree with the RAM-read pattern table exactly - blue nothing, yellow Cardmon, green water Digimon. The PLAYER side is decoded too (FISH-009): casting puts the player in leader mode 0x48 for the whole cast (jump table 0x80083590 entry 0x48 = 0x8009092c, six sub-states off 0x800836d8) - SETANIM 0x11 (cast), then on the SETANIM completion flag PLAYER09 + 0x13 (follow-through), then PLAYER10 + 0x14 (the waiting pose, held for the whole minigame), then on the cast resolving a silent-subtype balloon actor + 0x12, then after 0x3c ticks close it + 0x15 (standing up), then back to leader mode 1 with the scene lock at 0x800a9dd8 dropped. Those five clip ids are defined by exactly ONE of the game's 179 sprite packs - the dedicated 70-frame fishing pack P002PLYF (LBA 970) - so the player must be rendering from it for the whole mode. Cast and strike are two different pad buttons: CROSS casts, and the bobber's only pad read masks 0x2000 (CIRCLE) for the strike. The end-of-cast bubble is the SAME balloon actor as the spot's proximity indicator, spawned silent (FISH-010) -- but NOT the same glyph: the result bubble's subtype is 1, so it draws glyph row 1 (FIELDCOM cells 1/2), while the spot's rod-and-splash is row 5 (cells 10/11), so FISH-010's identity clause is contradicted.
